headline: Observation is intentional seeing—noticing what's actually there rather than what you expect
universal_truth: Seeing is not the same as looking; intentional observation reveals what casual glances miss
fun_facts: Sherlock Holmes' famous deductions were based on careful observation others missed
Doctors who look at X-rays miss obvious problems when they're not looking for them
Artists train observation skills that let them see colors and shapes others don't notice
discussion_questions: When do you really observe versus just look?
What do you miss because you're not paying attention?
How could better observation improve your decisions?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Looking is passive. Observation is active—intentionally noting what's present, not just what you expected. Most people look without seeing. Observers catch what others miss because they're paying attention on purpose.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We're constantly looking but rarely observing. What's the difference and why does it matter?

options.text: Observation is active attention—it sees what's actually there rather than what you expect; looking uses mental shortcuts; observing questions them
options.response: Yes. We usually see what we expect to see. Observation means setting expectations aside and noticing what's actually present. Reality is richer than our assumptions about it.

options.text: Some people are just more observant
options.response: Observation skill varies, but it's trainable—anyone can learn to see more carefully...

q1.title: Beyond Expectations
q1.script: We see what we expect—it's efficient but limiting. Observation means questioning expectations: 'What's actually here?' This reveals surprises, anomalies, and opportunities.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Beyond Expectations"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Trainable Skill
q2.script: Observation is a skill that improves with practice. Artists see colors you miss. Doctors see symptoms you'd overlook. Train your observation in domains that matter to you.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Slowing Down
q3.script: Observation requires slowing down. Quick glances use shortcuts. Careful observation takes time. What you gain in speed, you lose in insight.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Seeing is not the same as looking. Intentional observation reveals what casual glances miss. Learn to really see.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 297. Tomorrow, we'll explore what the evidence means—interpretation. Until then, practice observing something carefully you usually just glance at.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Observation Practice - What Are You Missing?
growTrack.activity: Choose something familiar—your commute, a room, a person you know. Observe it carefully for 5 minutes as if seeing it for the first time. What do you notice that you usually miss? Practice active observation.
